newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Treasury has draft for retirement scheme.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Treasury has draft for retirement scheme.

text.p: The Israeli Finance Ministry is circulating a draft proposal to allow individual retirement accounts (IRAs) in Israel for the first time, Treasury sources said.

Under the proposals, drawn up by the Treasury's capital markets division and being studied by the commercial banks, Israelis would have the choice of managing their own account, giving it to a portfolio manager or placing it in a joint account or fund. Savers would be free to join and leave the fund when they choose.
Treasury officials said the proposals are expected to go into effect at the start of next year.

The IRAs will be subject to the same tax benefits and other rules covering existing retirement schemes, called provident funds. Among other things, the IRAs will be required to hold at least 40 percent of their assets in Treasury bonds and bills, deposits or cash.
The IRA proposal is in line with the Treasury's long-term goal of opening of the capital markets to greater competition between financial advisers and to encourage long-term savings.
In addition, the provident funds have performed poorly in the past year and as a result have suffered massive redemptions from savers.
